correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the operator, positivity, all quantifiers, and the full coupling range. The critical nonstandard step is exact: positivity forces \(0<kd_j<\pi\), which makes the cyclic Dirichlet-to-Neumann off-diagonal weights positive; Perron--Frobenius then identifies \(lpha\) with the largest matrix eigenvalue. The constant-vector Rayleigh quotient is exactly \((2k/N)\sum_j	an(kd_j/2)\), strict Jensen applies on \((0,\pi/2)\), and \(2k	an(\pi k/N)\) is strictly increasing on the entire ground-state branch. The bundled transfer-matrix verifier checks independent secular residuals for multiple \(N\) and \(lpha\); finite checks are not used to infer the theorem.

originality.rationale: The primary paper explicitly leaves the every-coupling repulsive periodic statement as Conjecture 5.1 after proving only weak- and strong-coupling regimes. Targeted published-finding corpus and published-web searches for the conjecture, its periodic-delta aliases, and stronger all-coupling statements did not return a covering result. The own ledger contains an earlier \(N=2\) solution only; the present theorem treats every \(N\ge2\) with an essentially \(N\)-dimensional Perron--Frobenius/Jensen argument. The residual risk is an unindexed equivalent result under different terminology.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent solution could exist in an unindexed source under different terminology such as Kronig--Penney optimization or periodic measure potentials. No such source was found in the targeted searches.
